column2: one should say and repeat them three times, in low, middle and high tones in turn, O sage, first uttering the pranava, in the order of creation, preservation and dissolution.
Then in order one should say "bhuh sannyastam," likewise "bhuvah sannyastam," and saying "suvah sannyastam," utter the word "sannyastam."
At the end of every mantra one should say the word "maya"; first uttering the pranava, one should recite the collective vyahritis.
Having offered the full oblation with the three verses beginning "bhuh svaha" and concluded, one should diligently repeat the Gayatri until the afternoon.
Having thus recited the praisha mantras with an attentive mind, and repeating "Fearlessness to all beings from me, svaha,"
one should take up water to the east and pour out a handful; then, plucking out the tuft of hair and the sacred thread with one's hand,
holding them, one should say the pranava and "bhuh," and "Go to the ocean"; then, uttering "svaha," with a handful of water

one should offer them into the water; then, consecrating the water three times with the praisha mantras and sipping it, one should come to the bank and leave one's garments and the like on the ground.
Facing north or east, one should walk more than seven steps; when he has gone a little distance, the teacher should say, "Stay, stay."
For the sake of dealings with the world, the teacher should give him with his own hand a loincloth and a staff, saying, "Revered one, accept these."
Having given the loincloth with a good string and then an ochre garment, and having covered him and sipped water twice, he should say, "You are my disciple."
Then he should utter the mantra "You are Indra's thunderbolt"; the disciple, entreating, should take the staff while reciting "sakhayah."
Then, going to the guru's side and remembering Shiva's lotus feet, he should prostrate like a staff on the ground three times, self-controlled.
Then, having performed the evening twilight worship preceded by bathing, and made the evening fire offering, he should silently inform his guru.
Before beginning the rite, taking auspicious cow-dung, he should make balls the size of a large amalaka fruit and dry them
in the rays of the sun alone; placing them in the midst of the fire at the start of the offering, when the offering is complete he should gather the ash and keep it safe.
Then the guru, taking the white ash born of the Viraja fire, should with it, in order, with the mantras beginning "agnir iti,"
touch the disciple's limbs from the head down to the feet; and with the five mantras beginning with Ishana, starting from the head, all over,
having taken it up according to rule, he should then make him wear the tripundra, with the tryayusha and tryambaka mantras, beginning from the head in order.
Then the excellent disciple, with a mind full of true devotion, should meditate on Shiva, companion of Uma, seated in the lotus of the heart.
Placing his hand on the disciple's head, the guru should utter the pranava three times into his right ear, together with its seer and the rest.
Then, showing compassion, the excellent guru should teach him the meaning of the pranava, together with knowledge of its six kinds of meaning.
He should prostrate to that guru on the ground like a staff twelve times; he should always be subject to him and perform no other rite.
Having cooked the charu in that fire, he should offer oblations of fuel-sticks, rice and ghee separately with the Raudra Sukta and the five mantras beginning with Sadyojata.
Then the guru should have that same disciple perform the morning observances and the rest, preceded by hearing and the other limbs, at the end of the japa.
And the disciple should perform worship there in that mandala called the Kailasa slab, by the path taught by Shiva.
If he is unable to worship the god daily, he should receive from the guru an auspicious crystal linga of the Lord with its pedestal.
Better that I give up my life, or even that my head be cut off, than that I should eat without worshipping the blessed three-eyed one.
Uttering this oath three times in the guru's presence, the disciple, firm of mind and bearing devotion to Shiva, should take it.
From then on, his mind ever diligent, he should worship Mahadeva with supreme devotion by the path of the five enclosures.
Salutations to Shri Ganesha.
Salutations to Shri Gauri and Shankara.

The glorious Shiva Mahapurana, book 6, chapter 14: the description of the pranava as the form of Shiva. Vamadeva said: Blessed six-faced one, ocean of the nectar of all knowledge, son of the lord of all the immortals, destroyer of the distress of those who bow,
the fourth and fifth meanings reveal the form of the guru, and the sixth meaning is the self of the disciple; thus the six kinds of meaning are proclaimed.
Of these I shall tell you the form of the mantra, best of sages, by merely understanding which a man becomes greatly wise.
The first vowel, the fifth vowel, then the last of the fifth group, and the bindu and nada — these five letters are declared by the Vedas, and not otherwise.
Their collective form is declared to be the beginning of the Veda, Om; the nada is the totality of all, and the four with the bindu
are established in their individual form in the pranava that denotes Shiva. Hear, wise one, its form as a yantra: that is itself the Shiva linga.
At the very bottom one should draw the pedestal; above it the first vowel; above that the letter u; above that the last of the pa group;
on its head the bindu, and above that one should draw the nada. When the yantra is complete, every desire is fulfilled.
Having thus drawn the yantra, one should encircle it with the pranava nine times, with the nada arising from it, ending in the nada.
I shall tell you the meaning concerning the deities, which is everywhere hidden, O sage, out of affection for you, Vamadeva, as Shankara spoke it.
What is the knowledge of the six kinds of meaning, said to grant what one desires? What are those six kinds of meaning, and what is that knowledge, lord?
The five subtle deities in the form of Brahman are to be known; these same are amplified as the forms of Shiva himself.
The mantra that denotes Shiva also denotes Shiva's form, since there is no absolute difference between the form and the one who has the form.
Shiva's body was described earlier, beginning with "crowned by Ishana"; hear now of his five faces.
Beginning with the fifth and proceeding in order from Sadyojata, ending with the upward one, Ishana, the five faces are declared.
Abiding in the fourfold arrangement of the god Ishana are the four forms of Brahman, from Purusha down to Sadya.
The collective of the five Brahmans is the one renowned as Ishana Brahman; its individual forms, O sage, are from Purusha to Sadyojata.
This circle, made of grace, is the cause of the five acts; it is of the nature of the supreme Brahman, subtle, changeless and free of affliction.
Grace too is twofold: one within the sphere of concealment and the rest, and the other, the lord's, giving beings liberation higher and lower.
These are declared to be the two acts of Sadashiva alone; and within grace too there are the five acts of the Lord, creation and the rest.
What is its subject, and what is the fruit of knowing it? Tell me all this that I have asked, Guha.
The circle made of grace, consisting of the Shantyatita kala and presided over by Sadashiva, is called the supreme state.
This very state is attained by ascetics of cultivated self who worship Sadashiva, their minds devoted to the pranava.
Having attained this very state, the lords of sages enjoy, together with him, the god in the form of Brahman, most abundant pleasures,
and at the coming of the great dissolution they attain equality with Shiva; such people never again fall into the ocean of worldly existence.
The eternal Shruti speaks of them as "in the world of Brahma." And this indeed is the totality of Shiva's lordship.
The Atharvashikha says, "endowed with all lordship"; they declare that the giving of all lordship belongs to him alone.
There is no state higher than the state of the chamaka; the expansion of the five Brahmans is indeed seen as the manifold world.
From the Brahmans thus arose the kalas held to begin with Nivritti, which are of the nature of the subtle elements and renowned as causes.
Of this manifold world of gross form, O you of good vows, that which stands fivefold is held to be the five Brahmans.
Not knowing this meaning, bewildered by the shastras of the bound, even now I am deluded by Shiva's maya, Mahasena.
Prakriti, skin, hand, touch and air — this five is pervaded by Brahman in the form of Purusha, lord of sages.
Ego, eye, foot, form and fire — this five is pervaded by Aghora Brahman.
Intellect, tongue, anus, taste and water — this five is always pervaded by Vamadeva Brahman.
Mind, nose, the organ of generation, smell and earth — this five is pervaded by Sadya Brahman; the world is made of the five Brahmans.
The pranava that denotes Shiva has been taught in the form of a yantra — the collective of the five letters and the four beginning with the bindu.
One should contemplate the yantra form by the path Shiva taught — the pranava, the supreme king of mantras, in the form of Shiva.
Drinking the elixir of the nectar of knowledge of Shiva's two feet, I shall somehow become free of delusion.
Looking long upon me with eyes moist with the nectar of compassion, show grace to me, who have taken refuge at your glorious lotus feet."

The first meaning is the form of the mantra, the second is that contemplated through the mantra; the third is the meaning concerning the deities, and after that the meaning concerning the manifold world;
Beginning with "Sadyojatam prapadyami" and ending with "Sadashivom," the Shruti declares the pranava to denote the five Brahmans.
There too, O sage, the deities beginning with Sadya are proclaimed; those five, of the nature of the supreme Brahman, ever bestow welfare.
Purusha, ear and speech, sound and space — this five is pervaded by Brahman in the form of Ishana, best of sages.
Hearing what the lord of sages said, the mighty one who bears the power of knowledge spoke words that strike great terror into other schools of thought.
Subrahmanya said: Listen, tiger among sages, to what you have respectfully asked: the knowledge of the great Lord through the collective and the individual.
I shall tell in detail that which consists in knowing the meaning of the pranava, through knowledge of the unity of the six kinds of meaning, O you of good vows.
Salutations to Shri Ganesha.
Salutations to Shri Gauri and Shankara.

The glorious Shiva Mahapurana, book 6, chapter 15: the description of the forms for worship. The Lord said: Next I shall tell you the excellent course of creation of the four beginning with Mahesha, from Sadashiva, O fair-faced one.
From a thousandth part of Maheshvara the form of Rudra was born, having the form of the Aghora face and ruling the principle of fire.
Joined on his left with the Shakti Gauri, he is the lord who accomplishes all destruction; his individual form is the four beginning with Shiva.
Shiva, Hara, Mrida and Bhava — this is known as the wondrous circle called destruction, most divine and supreme, O lord of sages.
That destruction is declared by the wise to be threefold, by the distinction of constant and the rest: the constant is the deep sleep of beings; the occasional is remembered as that of Brahma;
and his dissolution is the great one, as the Veda shows. For the rest of beings wearied by the sorrows of birth and the like,
for their repose, best of sages, and for the ripening of their deeds, destruction has been devised in three ways by Rudra of boundless power.
These three are declared to be the acts of Rudra alone; and even within destruction there are the five acts of the Lord, creation and the rest.
There, O sage, the deities beginning with Bhava are proclaimed, of the nature of the supreme Brahman and bestowing grace on the worlds.
This circle called destruction consists of the Vidya kala, and is presided over by Rudra; this state is free of affliction.
Sadashiva is the collective, the lord ruling over space; the four beginning with Mahesha are his individual forms.
From a thousandth part of the form of Rudra came the birth of Vishnu; his self is the circle of Vamadeva, and he is sole ruler of the principle of water.
Joined on his left with the Shakti Rama, he is the great protector of all, four-armed, lotus-eyed, dark, bearing the conch and other emblems.
His individual forms are the four beginning with Vasudeva, which give liberation to the Vaishnavas devoted to worship:
Vasudeva, Aniruddha, then Sankarshana, and Pradyumna — this is renowned as the unsurpassed circle of preservation.
Preservation is the sustaining of the created world together with its creator, until the end of the enjoyment of the karma that has begun for beings who reap the fruits.
This is declared to be the act of Vishnu alone, who ordains protection; and even within preservation there are the five acts of the Lord, creation and the rest.
There the deities headed by Pradyumna are proclaimed, free of doubt, free of fear, ever giving the bliss of liberation.
This circle of preservation, O brahmin, of the excellent nature of Pratishtha and presided over by Janardana, is called the supreme state.
This very state is to be attained by those who serve Vishnu's lotus feet; this circle of the Vaishnavas grants the states of salokya and the rest.
From a thousandth part of Sadashiva came the birth of Mahesha; because of the endless form of Purusha, he is ruler of air.
Joined on his left with the goddess of speech, he is the creator, lord of the world, four-faced, red in colour, of the nature of rajas.
His individual forms are the four beginning with Hiranyagarbha: Hiranyagarbha, Virat, Purusha and Kala.
This circle of creation, O brahmin, served by the sages who are Brahma's sons and others, grants all desires and aims and gives happiness with one's family.
Creation is the bringing out into nature of the being that had been withdrawn, for the sake of experiencing its karma,
and joining it with the means, limbs and fruits; this act they know as the Grandsire's — those who understand the process of creating the world and the arrangement that brings happiness.
Even in the creation of the world, O sage, there are the five acts of the Lord; there Kalodaya and other deities are proclaimed.
This circle of creation is declared by the wise to be of the nature of Nivritti; presided over by the Grandsire, this state is splendid.
This very state is to be attained by men whose minds are offered to Brahma; for the Grandsire's devotees it gives liberation of salokya and the rest.
In this set of four circles too the pranava applies; in the order beginning with Mahesha it denotes them by a secondary sense.
Joined on his left with the Shakti Maya, he is with parts and excels in action; his individual forms are the four beginning with Ishvara:
The circle of the world is one, unfolded by Shambhu's Shakti; with its five members, creation and the rest, it is called five-spoked.
Like the whirling of a firebrand circle, it turns round with unbroken dissolution and arising; therefore it is called a circle.
Since it is the broad creation of creation and the rest, it appears broad; it belongs to the golden god Shambhu of boundless radiance.
This circle, the work of Shakti, rests on the golden light; it is enveloped by water, and the water by fire;
the fire is enveloped by air, the great one by space; space likewise by the elements' source, and that by the Mahat;
and the Mahat by the unmanifest — thus it is declared the cosmic egg by teachers who believe, best of sages.
Seven enclosures are declared for the protection of this universe; the water is ordained to be ten times greater than the circle,
and so each one above the other is ten times greater; this is to be known as the cosmic egg by those who understand, leader of sages.
Accepting this meaning, since it lies near the circle, the Shruti itself says "in the midst of the water."
Isha, Vishveshvara, then Paramesha, and after that Sarveshvara — this is the excellent circle of concealment.
What need of saying much here? I tell you the essence, O sage: it is certain that all this is Shiva alone, the possessor of Shakti.
Concealment is divided in two: one within the sphere of Rudra and the rest, and the other, by way of embodiment, for the continuance of the host of bound souls.
This very state is to be attained by those who serve Mahesha's feet; for the Maheshvaras it gives liberation by stages beginning with salokya.
This very state is to be attained by those who long to worship Rudra; for the Rudra-devotees it gives union by stages beginning with salokya, O sage.
From a thousandth part of Vishnu arose the Grandsire, whose self is the Sadyojata face and who rules the principle of earth.
This circle of the world, whose glory is renowned in the Shruti — the Shruti praises it as "the five-spoked wheel," O sage.
Through grace, concealment, destruction, preservation and creation, Shiva, one and joined with Shakti, ceaselessly carries on his play.
It is intent on colouring beings with enjoyment until the moment when their karma is balanced; when karma is balanced, the one Lord becomes full of grace.
There the deities called Sarveshvaras are proclaimed, of the very nature of the supreme Brahman, free of doubt and of affliction.
The circle of concealment consists of the Shanti kala, and is presided over by Maheshvara; this state is unsurpassed.
Salutations to Shri Ganesha.
Salutations to Shri Gauri and Shankara.
The glorious Shiva Mahapurana.

Om, salutation to Shiva. The sixth book, the Kailasa Samhita, chapter 16: the description of the principle of Shiva. Suta said: Having heard the meaning of the Veda taught by his guru, the eminent sage, having a doubt about the supreme self, respectfully asked:
Having uprooted the poison tree called doubt, born of ignorance, may my mind become the ground of the great wish-granting tree of Shiva's non-duality;
enlighten me, O God, by your grace; by your grace, lord of gods, I shall become firm in knowledge."
Subrahmanya said: This very secret, O sage, was spoken by Shiva while the Mother, the Goddess, listened, and I too, Vamadeva.
Then, drinking her milk and satisfied again and again, I heard it steadily, and it was reflected upon and settled by me.
I will tell it to you out of kindness, Vamadeva, great sage; hear now, son, this great and supreme secret.
There is ritual action, and beginning from the principles there is a very extensive doctrine of the shastras; the knower should hear, with discrimination, what gives knowledge, O sage.
Among the disciples you have taught, who is equal to you? Those base ones still wander among the shastras of Kapila and others.
They were cursed long ago by six sages for being given to reviling Shiva; their talk should not be heard, for they speak otherwise.
Vamadeva said: Master who bears the power of knowledge, whose body is supreme bliss, I have drunk the nectar of the meaning of the pranava flowing from your glorious lotus mouth.
Here too, O you of good vows, they speak of the fieriness of the mountain; since the manifold world is perceptible, the basis of perception is from it.
The supreme Lord, the supreme self, is to be known, without doubt. The universe, made of female and male forms, is seen by direct perception.
The body consists of six sheaths; of them the first three arise from the mother's portion and the others from the father's portion, so says the Shruti.
Just as people know female and male natures in all bodies, so the wise know a female and male nature in the supreme self too, O sage.
The Shruti speaks of Brahman as being, consciousness and bliss. The word "sat," which excludes non-being, is said to be of the nature of being.
The exclusion of insentience is made by the word "chit." The word "sat," which can take three genders, should here be taken as masculine.
It means light, clearly "sat" is light; the word "chit," a synonym of the word "knowledge," has become feminine.
Light and consciousness as a pair have become the cause of the world; and when the self of being and consciousness likewise becomes the cause of the world,
it is held that Shiva and Shakti are in one place. Even light has impurity from the oil, the wick and the like;
I have become firm in understanding and my doubt is gone. I ask you something more, Mahasena; hear me, lord.
The power of consciousness resting in the individual self always has weakness; to remove it, Shakti-hood is here eternal.
The usage "strong" and "possessing power" is constantly seen in the world and in the Veda, Vamadeva, great sage.
Thus Shiva-hood and Shakti-hood have been shown in the supreme self; from the union of Shiva and Shakti bliss constantly arises.
Therefore, O sage, with him as their aim, sages whose impurities were destroyed fixed their minds on Shiva and attained Shiva, free of affliction.
Thus the all-selfhood of those two is sung in the Upanishads as Brahman — by the word "Brahman," in the sense of the root brih.
Expanding and vastness belong to the body called Shambhu; the perception of the universe as made of the five Brahmans is called "Brahman."
I shall tell you, Vamadeva, out of affection, how the pranava arises from the reversal of "hamsa"; listen attentively.
By dropping the consonants s and h, "Om" alone remains, the gross word that denotes the supreme self.
It is to be known as the great mantra by sages who see the truth; within it is the subtle great mantra — I shall tell you how it is drawn out.
The existence of the world, whose form extends from Sadashiva down to a worm, is seen everywhere in female and male forms, without doubt.
The reversal of "hamsa" is "so'ham"; the meaning of s is remembered as Shiva; it is determined that what is denoted by the great mantra is of the nature of Shakti.
But at the time of the guru's teaching, "so'ham" means Shiva of the nature of Shakti; the great mantra then refers to the individual self, the bound soul.
Of the nature of Shakti and a portion of Shiva, through oneness with Shiva he shares equality with Shiva. In the great saying "Prajnanam Brahma," the meaning of prajnana is seen.
The word prajnana is a synonym of consciousness, without doubt; "consciousness is the self," O sage — thus the Shiva Sutra was set forth.
Consciousness is the nature of all knowledge and action in the universe; that whose nature is freedom is declared to be the self.
I have given you the commentary on the Shiva Sutras beginning thus. "Knowledge is bondage" — this is the second sutra of the Lord.
Knowledge here is the self's limited knowledge and action; with the first word the Lord states the characteristic of the host of bound souls.
These two were the first vibration of the supreme Shakti; this same supreme Shakti the Shvetashvatara school
joyfully praised as "natural, knowledge, strength and action"; they know Shambhu's three sights as knowledge, action and will.
What is the eternal cause of the world of such a form — is it female, or male, or neuter,
Therefore it is settled that this is the form of the self alone. I shall tell the meaning concerning the manifold world, showing its oneness with the pranava.
Om — all this is Om, says the eternal Shruti; therefore, beginning with "from that," the creation of the world is proclaimed.
I shall tell you the purport of that Shruti — listen — out of affection for you, Vamadeva, unfolded for the sake of discrimination.
It is settled that the union of Shiva and Shakti is the supreme self. From the supreme Shakti arose the power of consciousness;
from that the power of bliss, from that the power of will, from that the power of knowledge, and the fifth, the power of action. From these arose the kalas beginning with Nivritti, O sage.
Nada and bindu are declared to arise from consciousness and bliss; from the power of will comes the letter m, from the power of knowledge the fifth vowel u,
and from the power of action the vowel a, lord of sages. Thus the origin of the pranava has been told; hear now the arising of the five Brahmans.
From Shiva arose Ishana, then Tatpurusha, then Aghora, then Vama, and then Sadyojata.
From this came the thirty-eight mothers of the alphabet. From Ishana arose the kala called Shantyatita; from Purusha the Shanti kala; the Vidya kala arose from Aghora;
or mixed, or something else? No decision has been reached on it; the learned, bewildered by the shastras, dispute it in many ways here.
Or is it the form of the self? Here too there is great doubt; both these are the wondrous subject of everyone's disputes.
There is no room here even for the use of inference; that applies to the seeing of smoke, with its five members.
Impurity and inauspiciousness are seen in the fire of the funeral pyre and the like; thus, as the remover of these, auspiciousness is enjoined by the Shruti.
When, in the first, the fifteenth and the sixteenth vowels, among the three, the great mantra comes at the beginning with the letter s,
Entering this, which lies within the mind and is the field of the senses' knowledge, the bound soul always knows and acts.
Pratishtha and Nivritti are held to arise from Vama and Sadya. From Isha, beginning with the power of consciousness, come the Lord's five pairs.
The first vibration of the great Lord, when he set about creating the world by his own will, is called the Shiva principle.
They shine constantly even in contracted form. For the bound soul, kala, vidya, raga, kala (time) and niyati — as these five principles, it becomes kala here.
The five are held to be the cause of the acts of grace and the rest, by wise sages who know it and reveal the highest truth.
In this five of the nature of kala and letter, which has become a pair through the relation of denoted and denoting, the five elements
arose in the order beginning with space, eminent sage; they know them to be made of the pairs, beginning with the first and ending with the fifth.
Space has sound as its sole quality; air has sound and touch; fire is said to have sound, touch and form as its chief qualities;
water is remembered as having sound, touch, form and taste; earth is remembered as rich in sound, touch, form, taste and smell.
This is declared to be the pervasiveness of the elements; being pervaded is the reverse, in the order beginning with smell.
This manifold world is proclaimed as consisting of the five elements — clearly Virat, the self of the total of all, the cosmic egg.
Beginning with the earth principle and ending with the Shiva principle in order, the individual self dissolves into the mass of principles and is merged.
Endowed with Shakti, at creation it comes forth again through Shakti and remains happily in the form of the gross manifold world until the dissolution.
The Shrutis that ordain the creation of the world, together with the world, and the gods Vishnu, Brahma and the rest, and the siddhas do not know it.
This very will is the Shakti principle, since it pervades all acts. In the pair of the powers of knowledge and action, when knowledge predominates, it is Sadashiva;
when action is in excess, know it to be the Maheshvara principle, lord of sages; the balance of the powers of knowledge and action is held to be the pure principle of Shuddhavidya.
In things that are his own limbs, there is the sense of difference that is the Maya principle. When Shiva, veiling his own form, preceded by supreme lordship,
by maya becomes the perceiver of all things, then he is called Purusha — "having created it" — so says the Shruti.
This one is the transmigrant, the bound soul deluded by maya, devoid of the knowledge of Shiva, his mind confused by many deeds.
Delusion arises only for this bound soul, who knows the world as not different from Shiva but himself as different; not for the lord.
Just as a magician, a yogi, has no confusion, so one whose lordship is made known by the guru becomes Shiva, a mass of consciousness.
All-doership, omniscience, fullness, eternity and all-pervasiveness —
these five powers of Shiva shine in contracted form.
Make known how they come to oneness, and this other point. The usage "I know" and "I do" is seen.
It becomes the cause of limited doership and the means of limited principle; that is vidya. Raga is what colours one with attachment to objects.
Time is what makes manifest the appearances of things and non-things; becoming the delimiter of sequence, it is called the source of the elements.
Niyati is the Lord's power that regulates: "This I must do, this not"; through its compulsion the bound soul falls.
Since these five veil his true form, they are called the five sheaths and are the inner means.
That is established as the self of all, and no one disputes it — arising from all bodies, senses, mind, intellect and ego.
Suta said: Having heard the question put thus by the sage, the lord, his face slightly smiling, spoke this secret, rooted in Vedanta.
Salutations to Shri Ganesha.
Salutations to Shri Gauri and Shankara.
The glorious Shiva Mahapurana.

Om, salutation to Shiva. The sixth book, the Kailasa Samhita, chapter 17: the teaching of the knowledge of Shiva's non-duality, and the account of creation. Vamadeva said: Earlier you said that Purusha stands below Niyati and above Prakriti; how is it now said otherwise,
The organs of knowledge are ear, skin, eye, tongue and nose; sound, touch, form, taste and smell are their objects,
declared for the organs of knowledge in the order of ear and the rest. Then from the sattvic ego the subtle elements arose in order.
These are called subtle by sages who see the truth. The organs of action, together with their functions, are to be known:
O brahmin sage, speech, hands, feet, anus and the organ of generation; their actions are called speaking, grasping, going, excretion and pleasure.
From the ego that is the source of the elements the subtle elements arose in order; these are the subtle forms of sound and the rest — so it stands.
From them in order arose space, air, fire, water and earth; these are to be known, tiger among sages, as the five elements.
Giving room, carrying, cooking, cohesion and supporting are declared to be their functions.
Vamadeva said: The creation of the elements was told earlier as from the kalas; how is it now told otherwise, Skanda? I have great doubt about this.
The Atma principle is the letter a, the Vidya principle is u, and the Shiva principle is m; so think of it, Vamadeva.
that he, contracted in form by maya, is below it, lord? Please cut away this doubt of mine truly, master.
Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, Maheshvara and Sadashiva — they are the very forms of Shiva, renowned in the Shruti.
So you said before, and now it is said otherwise, that they arise from the subtle elements; I have great doubt about this.
Show your compassion, Skanda, and cut away my doubt. Hearing the sage's words, Kumara replied.
Shri Subrahmanya said: In the order of the creation of the elements beginning with "from that," O sage, hear them, great wise one, attentively and with respect.
It is certain that the five elements were born from the kalas; they are the forms of the gross manifold world, the body of the lord of beings.
In the order of the rising of the principles, from the Shiva principle down to earth, it should be said in order that they arise from the subtle elements, O sage.
The unity of the subtle elements and the kalas too is the cause of the elements; know that there is no contradiction here, best of the knowers of Brahman.
In the universe of gross and subtle nature arose the planets, moon, sun and the rest, with the stars, and other hosts of luminaries;
the deities Brahma, Vishnu, Mahesha and others, the classes of beings, the guardians of the directions headed by Indra, the gods, ancestors and asuras,
Shri Subrahmanya said: This doctrine of non-dual Shaivism never tolerates duality; duality is perishable, and the non-dual Brahman is supreme and imperishable.

Whatever things there are, all are established here; this should be reflected on with a sound mind, not outwardly, best of sages.
This universe of female and male forms, made of Shiva and Shakti, is to be worshipped by the wise like you, versed in the knowledge of Shiva.
One should worship all as Brahman, and "All indeed is Rudra," says the Shruti, O sage; therefore Sadashiva is the self of the manifold world.
By the power of placing the thirty-eight kalas, from contemplating duality, the guru whose self is cultivated with "I alone am Sadashiva" is Shiva.
A true disciple who reflects thus becomes a guru, Shiva himself, whose self is the manifold world, the deities, the yantra and the mantra; there is no doubt.
By the teacher's grace, O brahmin, all his bonds cut away, the disciple devoted to Shiva's feet surely becomes one with the guru.
Whatever thing exists, all of it, whether taken together or separately, by the predominance of qualities, they declare to be the meaning of the pranava.
Free of passion and other faults, the essence of the Veda spoken by Shiva — this knowledge of non-duality, dear to Shiva, I have lovingly told you.
Shiva is all-knowing and all-doing, lord of all, beyond qualities, father of the three gods, Brahman, whose body is being, consciousness and bliss.
I will surely cut off the head of that wicked one without hesitation, with my true Shakti like the fire of time to enemies; there is no doubt.
You yourself, O sage, are the best of the knowers of Shiva's non-duality, one who shows Shiva's conduct in teaching the knowledge of Shiva.
By contact with the ash of your body a great impure pishacha, his mass of sins cut away, attained by your grace the goal of the good.
You are known as a Shiva-yogi, whose glory is renowned in the three worlds; by contact with your glance a bound soul would become the lord of souls.
Your question to me about it was made respectfully for the instruction of the world; the good wander here for the benefit of the world.
Therefore this supreme secret is established in you. You too, with faith and devotion, in the pranavas with respect,
seat all of them, join them to the supreme Lord, and make them take up Shiva's conduct together with ash and rudraksha.
You are Shiva, following Shiva's conduct, having attained the state of non-duality; wandering for the protection of the world, attain imperishable happiness.

That same god Shankara, by his own will and his own maya, as if contracted in form, became Purusha.
Made an enjoyer by the five beginning with kala, this Purusha, abiding in Prakriti, enjoys the qualities born of Prakriti.

Om, salutation to Shiva. The sixth book, the Kailasa Samhita, chapter 18: the rite of making a disciple in the procedure of renunciation. Shaunaka said: Having heard that supremely wondrous secret, the essence of Vedanta, what did Vamadeva then ask the son of Maheshvara?
Shri Subrahmanya said: I shall tell you of the yoga-patta, by which one becomes a guru — out of affection for you, Vamadeva — a great secret that gives liberation.
In the month of Vaishakha, Shravana, Ashvina, Kartika, Margashirsha or Magha, in the bright fortnight, on an auspicious day,
on the fifth day or the full moon, having performed the morning rites, having received the guru's leave and bathed, with a controlled mind,
having cleansed the couch and wiped the body with that cloth, tying on a double string and putting on two garments,
his feet washed and having sipped water twice, he should take ash with the mantras beginning with Sadya and wear it by the method of smearing.
Held by the hand by the favourable guru, O sage, that disciple, his two hands folded, facing east,
should remain seated thus in the adorned pavilion on the guru's excellent pure seat covered with cloth, deerskin and kusha grass.
Then the teacher, taking a conch with its stand and purifying it with the astra mantra, should place it before him, favourably disposed.
Having worshipped the conch with its stand with flowers and the like, he should pour into it good water purified with the astra and kavacha mantras.
Blessed is the yogi Vamadeva, ever devoted to the knowledge of Shiva, through whom this divine and supremely purifying story arose.
Having filled it and worshipped it as before in the order stated for the six limbs, he should consecrate it again seven times with the pranava.
Worshipping it with fragrance, flowers and the like, showing incense and lamp, protecting the conch with the astra mantra, he should then veil it with the kavacha mantra.
Then the teacher should show the gestures called the cow and the conch; and again, before himself, to the right, in an excellent place,
by the rule stated for the arghya of worship, he should make a beautiful auspicious mandala and worship it with fragrant flowers and the like.
A pot with its stand, purified, clean, wound with thread, fumigated, set down and filled with pure scented water —
he should smear it with a fragrant mixture of the five barks, the five leaves and the five clays, lord of sages.
Then he should adorn that pot with cloth, mango leaves, tips of durva grass, a coconut, flowers and other things.
He should place the five gems in that pot, lord of sages, or in their absence place gold with devotion.
The gem called sapphire, ruby, gold, coral and gomedaka — these are remembered as the five gems.
Uttering "nrimluska" and "glum" at the end, the teacher, favourably disposed, should worship it lovingly and properly according to rule.
Hearing these words of the sages, full of love, the wise Suta, his mind devoted to Shiva, spoke to them, pleased.
Offering sweet rice, betel and the rest as before, and completing the worship with the eight names, he should consecrate it,
with a hundred and eight pranavas and the five Brahman mantras in order, from Sadya to Ishana, and with the astra mantra, protected again with the kavacha.
Veiling it and devoutly showing incense and lamp, he should properly show the gestures called the cow and the yoni there.
Then the teacher, covering the disciple's head with darbha grass, should mark out a square in the north-eastern part of the mandala.
Having arranged a lovely seat upon it according to rule, he should, favourably disposed, seat that disciple, the newly born one, there.
